tests.title: repomap.Build is exported with the correct signature and returns a non-empty map for a non-trivial workspace
given: a tools.Workspace rooted at a temp directory containing three Go source files in two directories
a budget of 6000 tokens
then: the returned error is nil
the returned string is non-empty and contains the file paths from the workspace
tests.pseudocode:
ws := newTestWorkspace(t, fixture3Files)
result, err := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 6000, nil)
assert.NoError(t, err)
assert.Contains(t, result, "phase.go")

tests.title: Build with budget 0 returns empty string and nil error without walking
given: a tools.Workspace rooted at a temp directory with files
then: the returned string is exactly ""
the returned error is nil
no file in the workspace was opened or walked (verified by a counting walk spy or by timing)
tests.pseudocode:
result, err := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 0, nil)
assert.Equal(t, "", result)
assert.NoError(t, err)

tests.title: Build delegates the file walk to tools.Walk so ignore rules and hidden-entry exclusion apply
given: a workspace with a .hidden directory, a .gitignore-d file, and two visible source files
then: the returned map contains the two visible source files
the returned map does not contain the hidden directory or the ignored file
tests.pseudocode:
result, _ := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 6000, nil)
assert.Contains(t, result, "visible.go")
assert.NotContains(t, result, ".hidden")
assert.NotContains(t, result, "ignored.go")

tests.title: Build extracts per-file top-level declarations via the outline package
given: a workspace with a Go file containing an exported function Foo at line 5 and a type Bar at line 12
then: the returned map contains 'func Foo L5'
the returned map contains 'type Bar L12'
tests.pseudocode:
result, _ := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 6000, nil)
assert.Contains(t, result, "func Foo L5")
assert.Contains(t, result, "type Bar L12")

tests.title: Build never returns a map whose token count exceeds the budget
given: a workspace with enough source files and declarations that the full map would exceed 200 tokens
then: afspec.EstimateTokens(result) <= 200
the returned error is nil
tests.pseudocode:
result, err := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 200, nil)
assert.NoError(t, err)
assert.LessOrEqual(t, afspec.EstimateTokens(result), 200)

tests.title: When outline.File fails for one file, Build includes that file without declarations and does not fail
given: a workspace with two Go files: one valid and one that causes outline.File to return an error (e.g. a binary file with .go extension or a corrupt syntax)
then: the returned error is nil
the returned string contains the path of the corrupt file (without declarations)
the returned string contains the valid file's path and its declarations
tests.pseudocode:
result, err := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 6000, nil)
assert.NoError(t, err)
assert.Contains(t, result, "corrupt.go")
assert.NotContains(t, result, "corrupt.go") // no declarations on that line
assert.Contains(t, result, "valid.go")
assert.Contains(t, result, "func ValidFunc")

tests.title: Build includes the directory tree and per-file declarations for all non-ignored, non-hidden files
given: a workspace with directories internal/agentrun/ and internal/toolio/, each containing one Go file with declarations
then: the returned map contains 'internal/agentrun/' and 'internal/toolio/' as directory lines
each file's declarations appear with kind, name and L-prefixed line number
tests.pseudocode:
result, _ := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 6000, nil)
assert.Contains(t, result, "internal/agentrun/")
assert.Contains(t, result, "internal/toolio/")
assert.Regexp(t, `func \w+ L\d+`, result)

tests.title: Files are sorted by path and declarations within a file are sorted exported-first then by line number
given: a workspace with a file containing: unexported func bar at L10, exported func Foo at L5, unexported func alpha at L1, exported type Baz at L20
then: in the output line for that file, Foo (L5) appears before Baz (L20), and both appear before alpha (L1) and bar (L10)
among the exported declarations, Foo (L5) appears before Baz (L20) — sorted by line
among the unexported declarations, alpha (L1) appears before bar (L10) — sorted by line
tests.pseudocode:
result, _ := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 6000, nil)
line := extractFileLine(result, "example.go")
idxFoo := strings.Index(line, "func Foo L5")
idxBaz := strings.Index(line, "type Baz L20")
idxAlpha := strings.Index(line, "func alpha L1")
idxBar := strings.Index(line, "func bar L10")
assert.Less(t, idxFoo, idxBaz)
assert.Less(t, idxBaz, idxAlpha)
assert.Less(t, idxAlpha, idxBar)

tests.title: The map contains no timestamps, file sizes or metadata other than path, declarations and collapsed-directory file counts
given: a workspace with several files of varying sizes and modification times
then: the returned string does not contain any date or time pattern (YYYY-MM-DD, HH:MM, epoch)
the returned string does not contain any byte-size pattern (e.g. '1024 bytes', '4.2KB')
tests.pseudocode:
result, _ := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 6000, nil)
assert.NotRegexp(t, `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}`, result)
assert.NotRegexp(t, `\d+ bytes`, result)
assert.NotRegexp(t, `\d+\.?\d*[KMG]B`, result)

tests.title: Same tree, same inputPaths and same budget produce a byte-identical map
given: a workspace with a fixture tree of 10+ files across 3+ directories
tests.when: for any budget in [100, 500, 1000, 6000] and any subset of inputPaths from the fixture's files, Build is called twice with the same arguments
then: the two returned strings are byte-identical

tests.title: The default budget of 6000 tokens is used when the flag's default value is passed
given: a workspace whose full map would be under 6000 tokens
then: the full map is returned with all declarations (no reduction applied)
afspec.EstimateTokens(result) <= 6000
tests.pseudocode:
result, _ := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 6000, nil)
assert.LessOrEqual(t, afspec.EstimateTokens(result), 6000)
assert.Contains(t, result, "func unexportedHelper") // unexported still present

tests.title: Reduction follows the deterministic order: drop unexported, drop test-file decls, drop deepest-dir decls, collapse deepest dirs
given: a workspace with a deep directory tree (4+ levels), test files, exported and unexported declarations, totalling well over 200 tokens when fully rendered
tests.when: repomap.Build is called with progressively smaller budgets: 2000, 1000, 500, 200
then: at 2000 tokens: unexported declarations are absent but exported ones remain
at 1000 tokens: test-file declarations are also absent
at 500 tokens: declarations from the deepest directories are absent before shallower ones
at 200 tokens: the deepest directories are collapsed to 'dir/ (N files)'
tests.pseudocode:
r2000, _ := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 2000, nil)
assert.NotContains(t, r2000, "func helper")
assert.Contains(t, r2000, "func Exported")
r1000, _ := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 1000, nil)
assert.NotContains(t, r1000, "func TestSomething")
r500, _ := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 500, nil)
assert.NotContains(t, r500, "func DeepExported")
r200, _ := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 200, nil)
assert.Regexp(t, `deep/ \(\d+ files\)`, r200)

tests.title: Directories named in inputPaths are reduced last among directories at the same depth
given: a workspace with two directories at the same depth: internal/important/ and internal/other/, each with declarations
inputPaths includes 'internal/important/file.go'
tests.when: repomap.Build(ctx, ws, budget, inputPaths) is called with a budget tight enough to force reduction
then: internal/important/'s declarations survive while internal/other/'s are dropped or collapsed first
tests.pseudocode:
result, _ := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, tightBudget, []string{"internal/important/file.go"})
assert.Contains(t, result, "func ImportantFunc")
assert.NotContains(t, result, "func OtherFunc")

tests.title: When the budget is large enough, the full map with all declarations and no collapsed directories is returned
given: a workspace with a small tree (5 files, ~50 declarations) whose full map is under 6000 tokens
then: every file's declarations appear in the output
no directory is collapsed (no '(N files)' pattern appears)
unexported declarations are present
tests.pseudocode:
result, _ := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 6000, nil)
assert.NotContains(t, result, "files)")
assert.Contains(t, result, "func unexportedHelper")
assert.Contains(t, result, "func ExportedFunc")

tests.title: Directories are rendered with trailing '/' and files are indented two spaces
given: a workspace with internal/agentrun/phase.go
then: the output contains a line matching 'internal/agentrun/'
the output contains a line starting with two spaces followed by 'phase.go'
tests.pseudocode:
result, _ := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 6000, nil)
assert.Regexp(t, `(?m)^internal/agentrun/$`, result)
assert.Regexp(t, `(?m)^  phase\.go`, result)

tests.title: Declarations are rendered on the same line as their file, separated by ' · ', with kind name and L-prefixed line
given: a workspace with a file containing func Run at line 240 and type Phase at line 148
then: the file's line contains 'type Phase L148 · func Run L240' or the declarations in the correct sorted order separated by ' · '
tests.pseudocode:
result, _ := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, 6000, nil)
line := extractFileLine(result, "phase.go")
assert.Contains(t, line, "type Phase L148")
assert.Contains(t, line, "func Run L240")
assert.Contains(t, line, " · ")

tests.title: A collapsed directory is rendered as 'dir/ (N files)' with the correct file count
given: a workspace with a deep directory containing 7 files, and a budget tight enough to collapse it
tests.when: repomap.Build(ctx, ws, tightBudget, nil) is called
then: the output contains 'deepdir/ (7 files)'
tests.pseudocode:
result, _ := repomap.Build(ctx, ws, tightBudget, nil)
assert.Contains(t, result, "deepdir/ (7 files)")

tests.title: The map block is placed under '## Repository map' with the correct opening sentence in the user prompt
given: a non-empty map string returned by repomap.Build
tests.when: a tool's prompt function (e.g. taskPrompt for issue) is called with the map
then: the user prompt contains '## Repository map'
the user prompt contains the opening sentence starting with 'The map below lists the repository'
the map block appears after landscape/steering blocks and before prior-phase conclusions
tests.pseudocode:
prompt := taskPrompt(input, root, repoMap)
assert.Contains(t, prompt, "## Repository map")
assert.Contains(t, prompt, "The map below lists the repository")
idxMap := strings.Index(prompt, "## Repository map")
idxPrior := strings.Index(prompt, "## The diagnosis") // or equivalent prior-phase block
assert.Less(t, idxMap, idxPrior)

tests.title: When the map is empty, the '## Repository map' block is absent and the prompt is byte-identical to one built without the map
given: an empty map string (budget was 0)
tests.when: a tool's prompt function is called with an empty map
then: the user prompt does not contain '## Repository map'
the user prompt is byte-identical to one built by the same function with no map parameter
tests.pseudocode:
promptWith := taskPrompt(input, root, "")
promptWithout := taskPromptLegacy(input, root) // or same function with empty map
assert.Equal(t, promptWith, promptWithout)
assert.NotContains(t, promptWith, "## Repository map")

tests.title: The map never appears in the envelope output
given: a completed run with a non-empty map
then: the envelope JSON does not contain the map string or '## Repository map'
the envelope JSON does not contain a 'repo_map' key
tests.pseudocode:
envelopeJSON := marshalEnvelope(result)
assert.NotContains(t, string(envelopeJSON), "## Repository map")
assert.NotContains(t, string(envelopeJSON), "repo_map")

tests.title: Common.Register registers --repo-map-tokens with default 6000 and stores it in RepoMapTokens
given: a new flag.FlagSet and a Common struct
tests.when: Common.Register is called and the flag set is parsed with no --repo-map-tokens argument
then: c.RepoMapTokens == 6000
the flag set recognises --repo-map-tokens as a valid flag
tests.pseudocode:
var c toolio.Common
fs := flag.NewFlagSet("test", flag.ContinueOnError)
c.Register(fs)
fs.Parse([]string{})
assert.Equal(t, 6000, c.RepoMapTokens)
// also parse with explicit value
fs2 := flag.NewFlagSet("test2", flag.ContinueOnError)
c2 := toolio.Common{}
c2.Register(fs2)
fs2.Parse([]string{"--repo-map-tokens", "0"})
assert.Equal(t, 0, c2.RepoMapTokens)

tests.title: Each tool passes --repo-map-tokens value as the budget argument to repomap.Build
given: a tool pipeline (issue, fix, spec or impl) configured with --repo-map-tokens 3000
tests.when: the pipeline builds its first phase
then: repomap.Build is called with budget=3000
the resulting Phase.RepoMap reflects a map built with that budget
tests.pseudocode:
// For each tool, set up with RepoMapTokens=3000 and a spy on repomap.Build
pipeline := newTestPipeline(t, toolio.Common{RepoMapTokens: 3000})
pipeline.Run(ctx)
assert.Equal(t, 3000, spiedBudget)

tests.title: With --repo-map-tokens 0, user prompts are byte-identical to those built without the map change
given: a tool's prompt function and a reference prompt built without any map support
tests.when: the prompt function is called with an empty map (from budget 0)
then: the resulting prompt is byte-identical to the reference prompt
tests.pseudocode:
refPrompt := buildReferencePrompt(input)
newPrompt := buildPromptWithMap(input, "")
assert.Equal(t, refPrompt, newPrompt)

tests.title: Phase struct has a RepoMap string field that can be set and read
given: an agentrun.Phase value
tests.when: Phase.RepoMap is set to a non-empty string
then: Phase.RepoMap returns the same string
tests.pseudocode:
p := agentrun.Phase{RepoMap: "test map"}
assert.Equal(t, "test map", p.RepoMap)

tests.title: Under --verbose, the runner logs the map's token count via Observer.Detail when RepoMap is non-empty
given: a Phase with a non-empty RepoMap of known length
a Runner configured with verbose=true and a recording Observer
then: Observer.Detail is called with a message containing the token count matching afspec.EstimateTokens(phase.RepoMap)

tests.title: The runner never injects Phase.RepoMap into the prompt itself
given: a Phase with RepoMap set to 'MARKER_STRING' and a User prompt that does not contain it
tests.when: the runner assembles and sends the prompt to the model
then: the user prompt sent to the model does not contain 'MARKER_STRING'
the system prompt sent to the model does not contain 'MARKER_STRING'
tests.pseudocode:
phase := agentrun.Phase{RepoMap: "MARKER_STRING", User: "do the thing"}
promptSent := capturePromptSentByRunner(runner, phase)
assert.NotContains(t, promptSent.User, "MARKER_STRING")
assert.NotContains(t, promptSent.System, "MARKER_STRING")

tests.title: issue pipeline builds the map once before the triage phase and passes it to the prompt builder
given: an issue pipeline with a workspace and --repo-map-tokens 6000
then: repomap.Build is called exactly once
the triage phase's RepoMap field is non-empty
the triage phase's User prompt contains '## Repository map'
tests.pseudocode:
spy := &buildSpy{}
pipeline := newIssuePipeline(t, spy)
pipeline.Run(ctx)
assert.Equal(t, 1, spy.callCount)
assert.NotEmpty(t, spy.lastResult)
assert.Contains(t, pipeline.phase.User, "## Repository map")

tests.title: spec pipeline builds the map once and reuses it for every scope of a split
given: a spec pipeline that splits into two scopes
then: repomap.Build is called exactly once
both scopes' PRD and generation phases receive the same map string
tests.pseudocode:
spy := &buildSpy{}
pipeline := newSpecPipeline(t, spy, 2) // 2 scopes
pipeline.Run(ctx)
assert.Equal(t, 1, spy.callCount)
assert.Equal(t, pipeline.scope1Map, pipeline.scope2Map)

tests.title: fix pipeline builds the map before analysis and rebuilds before implementation only if the tree changed
given: a fix pipeline where the analysis phase does not change the tree but the implementation phase does
then: repomap.Build is called once before analysis
the tree-change check runs before implementation
if HEAD or dirty files changed, Build is called again; otherwise the same map is reused

tests.title: impl pipeline builds the map before survey and rebuilds before each subsequent phase only if the tree changed
given: an impl pipeline with 3 tasks where task 1 commits (changing HEAD) and task 2 does not
tests.when: the pipeline runs survey, task 1, task 2, task 3
then: Build is called before survey (1st call)
Build is called before task 2 because task 1 changed HEAD (2nd call)
Build is NOT called before task 3 because task 2 did not change the tree
total Build calls = 2
tests.pseudocode:
spy := &buildSpy{}
gitSpy := &gitStateSpy{headChangesAfterTasks: []int{1}} // HEAD changes after task 1 only
pipeline := newImplPipeline(t, spy, gitSpy, 3)
pipeline.Run(ctx)
assert.Equal(t, 2, spy.callCount)

tests.title: Tree change is detected by comparing HEAD and dirty files against the values at the last build
given: a recorded state of HEAD='abc123' and dirtyFiles=['a.go']
a current state of HEAD='def456' and dirtyFiles=['a.go', 'b.go']
tests.when: the tree-change detector compares current vs recorded
then: it reports that the tree changed (HEAD differs)
tests.pseudocode:
detector := repomap.NewTreeChangeDetector(git)
detector.Record(ctx) // records abc123, [a.go]
// simulate commit
git.setHead("def456")
git.setDirty(["a.go", "b.go"])
assert.True(t, detector.Changed(ctx))

tests.title: When the tree-change check fails, the map is rebuilt unconditionally and no error surfaces
given: a git instance that returns an error from Head (e.g. not a git repo)
tests.when: the tree-change detector is asked whether the tree changed
then: the detector reports changed=true (triggering a rebuild)
no error is returned to the caller
the phase receives a freshly built map
tests.pseudocode:
git := &failingGit{headErr: errors.New("not a git repo")}
detector := repomap.NewTreeChangeDetector(git)
changed, err := detector.Changed(ctx)
assert.True(t, changed)
assert.NoError(t, err)

tests.title: When repomap.Build returns an error, the phase runs without a map and a low warning with code repo_map_build_failed is emitted
given: a pipeline where repomap.Build is stubbed to return an error
then: the phase proceeds with an empty RepoMap
the run does not fail
the envelope's warnings array contains a warning with code 'repo_map_build_failed' and level 'low'
tests.pseudocode:
spy := &buildSpy{err: errors.New("walk failed")}
pipeline := newIssuePipeline(t, spy)
result := pipeline.Run(ctx)
assert.True(t, result.OK)
assert.Equal(t, "", pipeline.phase.RepoMap)
assert.Contains(t, result.Warnings, toolio.Warning{Code: "repo_map_build_failed", Level: "low"})

tests.title: WarnRepoMapBuildFailed constant exists with value 'repo_map_build_failed' and is registered in warnStages
given: the toolio/warncode.go file
then: the returned stage is a non-empty string (the tool's first phase name)
ok is true
WarnRepoMapBuildFailed's string value is 'repo_map_build_failed'
tests.pseudocode:
assert.Equal(t, toolio.WarnCode("repo_map_build_failed"), toolio.WarnRepoMapBuildFailed)
stage, ok := toolio.WarnStage(toolio.WarnRepoMapBuildFailed)
assert.True(t, ok)
assert.NotEmpty(t, stage)

tests.title: Golden-file test: map at multiple budget steps matches pinned output
given: a fixture workspace with a known set of files and declarations
golden files for budgets 6000, 1000, 300
tests.when: repomap.Build is called at each budget
then: each result is byte-identical to its golden file

tests.title: issue builds a map and injects it into the triage prompt end-to-end
given: a git repository with Go source files containing declarations
the issue tool configured with --repo-map-tokens 6000
tests.when: the issue pipeline runs against the repository with a problem report
then: repomap.Build is called with the workspace and budget 6000
the triage phase's user prompt contains '## Repository map' with the opening sentence
the map contains file paths and declarations from the repository
the phase runs successfully

tests.title: impl rebuilds the map when the tree changes between tasks
given: a git repository with a spec containing two tasks
the impl tool configured with --repo-map-tokens 6000
tests.when: the impl pipeline runs: survey, task 1 (which commits new files), task 2
then: the map is built before the survey phase
after task 1 commits, HEAD changes and the map is rebuilt before task 2
task 2's prompt contains declarations from files task 1 created

tests.title: budget 0 disables the map and produces identical prompts
given: a git repository with Go source files
the spec tool configured with --repo-map-tokens 0
then: repomap.Build returns an empty string without walking
no phase's user prompt contains '## Repository map'
the prompts are byte-identical to those produced without the map feature

tests.title: map build failure degrades gracefully — phase runs without a map and warning is emitted
given: a git repository where outline.File fails on a corrupt source file causing repomap.Build to return an error
then: the analysis phase runs without a '## Repository map' block in its prompt
the run does not fail due to the map build error
the envelope's warnings array contains a warning with code 'repo_map_build_failed'

tests.title: spec reuses the map across all scopes of a split
given: a git repository with Go source files
the spec tool configured with --repo-map-tokens 6000
an input that the PRD phase splits into two scopes
tests.when: the spec pipeline runs both scopes
then: repomap.Build is called exactly once
both scopes' PRD and generation phases contain the same '## Repository map' block
the map strings are byte-identical across scopes
